standard_prerequisites.name: The exact sequence 0 to I cap J to R to R/I plus R/J
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Written down at the first line of the counted proof (line 8867)
standard_prerequisites.use: Presents the intersection of the two ideals as the kernel of a map out of R.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness as exactness of tensoring
standard_prerequisites.use: Preserves the exact sequence after tensoring with M, so that the intersection is carried into (I cap J) tensor M.

core_obligations: Write the intersection I cap J as the kernel of the natural map R to R/I plus R/J and obtain the resulting short exact sequence (proof line 8867).
Tensor that sequence with the flat module M, which keeps it exact, and identify the map M to M/IM plus M/JM (proof lines 8868-8871).
Compute the kernel of the resulting map as IM cap JM and conclude that it equals (I cap J)M (proof lines 8872-8873).
proof_roadmap: Encode the intersection by an exact sequence of ideals in R (proof line 8867).
Use flatness to tensor the sequence and read the intersection of images as the image of the intersection (proof lines 8868-8874).
difficulty_reason: For ideals I, J in a ring R and a flat R-module M the lemma states IM cap JM = (I cap J)M (statement lines 8860-8864). The proof does not choose generators or argue with elements: it writes the intersection as the kernel of the diagonal map R to R/I plus R/J, tensors this exact sequence with M, and reads the kernel of the tensor product M to M/IM plus M/JM as IM cap JM (proof lines 8866-8874). The two identifications that make the argument work, namely that flatness keeps the sequence exact and that the kernel of the tensor product is the intersection of the two submodules, are both used explicitly. H2.
